issues.claim: R5-05 (b) set a budget: a change of the drawn week re-evaluates the chips within ≈ 100 ms of the frame being drawn, at the METROPOLIS cap. Rendering wrote it at §12.5 (base l. 17176–17179) and at T-ER-25's bar (l. 14753): "the chips re-evaluated within ≈ 100 ms of each scrubbed frame being drawn … the scrub clauses from the later of M5 and V06's E6". It also wrote it at §12.10's R12-35 (l. 17527). R12-35 names its measure as "V12 §3.15.10's `time.findSuggest` and `time.findGlow` (the glow from a chip's click, and from a scrubbed week's frame being drawn) … the scrubbed week's from the later of M5 and V06's E6", with the bar "≤ 100 ms (T120-6; T-ER-25)". The other two homes of the same timing still time only the click. The bar R12-35 cites, T120-6 (l. 18662–18663), reads "a chip's glow within ≈ 100 ms of its click (`time.findSuggest`, `time.findGlow` …)". §13.8's T120-6 row (l. 19373) reads "M5". V12's statistic follows the base bar: its catalogue row (V12 l. 1172) reads "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn", and §3.15.10's T120-6 bullet (l. 2641–2643) says the same. T-V12-52 (l. 3174), which takes T120-6, plants no re-evaluation time and runs at M5 alone. VRC4T-04 asked that "R12-35's row and T120-6 add that timing", and R5-05's sweep lists "R12-35 and T120-6". Part H gives no END line for T120-6, which is scope's text. Rendering's two hand-offs, to scope and to V12, are open (repair-r5-rendering l. 133–141). V12 declined to write ahead of its home (repair-r5-V12, "Hand-offs received"). So the register's third bar reads a measurement that V12's statistic, as specified, never takes. A builder following V12 times only clicks. A builder following R12-35 also times the scrubbed frame. MAJOR: two builders build different behaviour, and the register needs an input that has no producer (VAP-r2-11's grade for a V12 statistic narrower than its base home).
issues.required_change: §13.2's T120-6, after "a chip's glow within ≈ 100 ms of its click": add ", and at a drawn week whose frame is not the head the chips re-evaluated within ≈ 100 ms of that frame being drawn, the frame never waiting for them (§12.5; that clause from the later of M5 and V06's E6, V06 §3.15.2's frames)". §13.8's T120-6 row's milestone cell "M5" → "M5 (its drawn-week clause at the later of M5 and V06's E6)". V12's end, for an END line: - The catalogue row (l. 1172), "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn" → "a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn, and a drawn week's frame (one that is not the head) drawn to its chips' re-evaluated glow drawn (from the later of M5 and V06's E6)". - §3.15.10's T120-6 bullet, "`time.findGlow` (a chip's click to its matches' glow drawn)" → "`time.findGlow` (a chip's click, and a scrubbed week's frame being drawn, to its matches' glow drawn — the latter from the later of M5 and V06's E6)". - T-V12-52, after "a planted suggestion time above §12.5's budget at the METROPOLIS cap fails its timing row": add "and a planted re-evaluation drawn more than 100 ms after a scrubbed week's frame fails `time.findGlow`'s". - T-V12-52's cell, "M5 (Find's milestone, §16)" → "M5 (Find's milestone, §16); its scrubbed-week glow at the later of M5 and V06's E6 (V06 §3.15.2's frames)".

issues.claim: R5-08 (c) gave a famine look a `field` read. V09 wrote its test into T-V9-85 (V09 l. 4436): "on a dossier crisis fixture with a famine at severity 0.5 (V08 §7.1), the why card of a bare field carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor` and that of a field left sown none". V08 §7.1's crisis fixtures (V08 l. 3242–3246) hold "… a famine, a fire, a flood and an earthquake … each standing through part of the year at its severity". They name no severity for the famine, and V12 §3.15.12 (l. 2693) and X-V12-5 restate them the same way. The clause needs a severity below 1, since at 1 every field is bare. V09's hand-off to V08 and V12 (repair-r5-V09 l. 120–122) is open. V12 declined it as V08's ("the severity belongs in V08 §7.1, which X-V12-5 then cites"). This is a fixture list that omits a case its test names, so the grade is minor (R5-01).
issues.required_change: V08 §7.1's crisis fixtures (l. 3244): "a plague with its affected quarter, a famine, a fire" → "a plague with its affected quarter, a famine at severity 0.5 (its look baring part of the arable faces and leaving the rest sown, V09's T-V9-85), a fire".

issues.claim: Round 5 changed the `item110.*` pin's H-AQUA suite. T-V6-65 (V06 l. 4188) now runs its pins "over H-100, H-AQUA (run without the two raised-way edits its fixture logs — the viaduct row's `editTable` and the declared elevated road — so that the overlay's off form governs it), H-TERRACE and H-DECK". R5-10 (VV56-r4-02) gave H-AQUA those two edits (V06 l. 4063–4072). A pin's overlay leaves the cells editable, so with the edits kept the history under the overlay would hold raised ways. V12 §2.13's `item110.*` row (V12 l. 922) still lists "H-100, H-AQUA, H-TERRACE, H-DECK (V06, T-V6-65)". V06 §7's E1 registration line (V06 l. 4275) reads "(H-100, H-AQUA, H-TERRACE, H-DECK; T-V6-65)". R3-26 makes V12 §2.13's suites column exactly the union of the registering clauses. V06's hand-off asks "a verifier checks that the two agree" (repair-r5-V06, HAND-OFFS), and they differ in form. The registering seat runs what T-V6-65 states, so nothing built changes. MINOR.
issues.required_change: V12 §2.13's `item110.raised`, `.terrace`, `.deck`, `.stepped` row (l. 922): "H-100, H-AQUA, H-TERRACE, H-DECK (V06, T-V6-65)" → "H-100, H-AQUA without its two raised-way edits (the CITY viaduct row's `editTable` and the declared elevated road), H-TERRACE, H-DECK (V06, T-V6-65)". V06's end, for an END line: §7's E1 line (l. 4275) "(H-100, H-AQUA, H-TERRACE, H-DECK; T-V6-65)" → "(H-100, H-AQUA without its two raised-way edits, H-TERRACE, H-DECK; T-V6-65)".

issues.claim: R5-06 (VAF-R4T-01) gave T-V7-69 (c) (V07 l. 3702) V01 §3.16 (5)'s count at the village rungs, with two cases: "on a VILLAGE fixture whose calamity names more ends than k (every named end struck) and on a fire whose order ends before k (the shortfall reported)". T-V7-69's fixture list holds neither. It names "THORP (P = 1, 40), HAMLET and VILLAGE (P = 1 499) fixtures — … each look kind previewed … and, from M-SF, a dossier fixture carrying each mapped condition, among them a disaster whose rebuild Works begin on some of an end's buildings inside its weeks". A preview has no targets, so it cannot name ends. A village fire's order ends before k only on a village where an end has no `neighbours` unit (V07 §5.6 (3), l. 3480–3485: no plot sharing a boundary or a way segment with another end's). No fixture is said to have that shape. This is R5-10's class: a test names a case that no fixture list carries, as VAP-r4-05 was at the town rungs, where V08 §7.1 now names `town-1`'s two banks. The test text states the cases, so the grade is minor.
issues.required_change: T-V7-69's fixture list: after "among them a disaster whose rebuild Works begin on some of an end's buildings inside its weeks" add "; and two test-side mutations of one of V07 §7's frozen small-dossier VILLAGE fixtures, each from M-SF — a calamity whose `targets` name uses on more ends than its severity's share k of the village's units, and a fire at severity 1 whose `targets` name a use on an end that no other end neighbours (V07 §5.6 (3)'s `neighbours`: an end parted from the rest by a water face or by land no plot of either touches), its order ending at that end before k, the harness asserting the end's isolation before the clause reads it".

issues.claim: V12 and V08 register derived dossier fixtures in §13.2's fixture manifest: - V12 §1b (V12 l. 207–209): "the derived fixtures registered in §13.2's frozen fixture manifest (item 84; §17.1 (3) makes it the one door for a dossier into `plat/`)". The population row (l. 211) gives "a derived fixture `<dossier>@pop×k` in the manifest". - V12's spec field `dossier` (l. 633): "a fixture id of the frozen manifest …, a derived '<dossier>@pop×k' included". - V12 l. 1419: a population sweep or a landmark "enters as a fixture record of the frozen manifest". - V08 W93 (V08 l. 320) and V08 §7 (l. 3354): "their `@pop×k` derivatives registered in the frozen manifest". - V08 §7.1 (l. 3242): V12's item-122 and item-125 fixtures are "test-side mutations made here (X-V12-5), each in §13.2's frozen manifest". This round added three such mutations: the `metropolis-3` cap copy, `city-1`'s second fire and `town-1`'s severity-1 fire (V08's hand-off to scope). The home cannot hold them. §13.2's manifest (base l. 18307–18316) "holds one row per file". `DossierFixtureRow.kind` is `'birth'|'after-events'|'after-ticks'|'world-state'`, with no derived kind and no field naming a source file and its mutation. V08 §7.1 also says a mutation is "never written back into a fixture file". So a harness built to the base has no row for `town-1@pop×2` or the crisis copies, and one built to V12 looks them up there. The derived content is stated in each case, so nothing built or tested changes. This is a list that omits an id its readers name, graded minor.
issues.required_change: §13.2's manifest paragraph: "Their `manifest.json` holds one row per file:" → "Their `manifest.json` holds one row per file, and one per derived fixture a volume names — a run-time, test-side mutation of one file, never written as a file (V12 §1b's `<dossier>@pop×k` levels; V08 §7.1's crisis, force and required-keys fixtures):". `DossierFixtureRow`'s `kind` union adds `'derived'`, and the interface adds `derivedFrom?: { file: string; mutation: string /* the mutation as its volume names it — '@pop×k', or the V08 §7.1 fixture's name */ } /* kind 'derived' only: its source row's file; the harness makes it at run time */`.
